objective.text: Understand which attacks HttpOnly mitigates without treating it as CSRF protection.

difficulty.rationale: Avoid assigning a cookie flag protections outside its browser contract.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: The session cookie is HttpOnly. A review proposes removing CSRF protection because JavaScript cannot read that cookie. What is the correct assessment?

options.text: Keep CSRF defenses only on GET routes because HttpOnly blocks cookies on POST.
options.rationale: Cookie transmission is not limited to GET by the HttpOnly flag.
options.misconception: Cookie transmission is not limited to GET by the HttpOnly flag.

options.text: Remove CSRF defenses because HttpOnly prevents all cross-origin requests.
options.rationale: The flag is not a cross-origin request firewall.
options.misconception: The flag is not a cross-origin request firewall.

options.text: Remove CSRF defenses because HttpOnly requires every request to include a password.
options.rationale: HttpOnly does not introduce per-request password authentication.
options.misconception: HttpOnly does not introduce per-request password authentication.

options.text: Keep CSRF defenses; HttpOnly blocks script reads but eligible requests can still carry the cookie.
options.rationale: Preventing direct access to the cookie value does not prevent the browser from attaching it to a request.

explanation.summary: Preventing direct access to the cookie value does not prevent the browser from attaching it to a request.
trace: Cookie transmission is not limited to GET by the HttpOnly flag.
The flag is not a cross-origin request firewall.
HttpOnly does not introduce per-request password authentication.
Preventing direct access to the cookie value does not prevent the browser from attaching it to a request.

contains: Forbids JavaScript from accessing the cookie
validation.reason: MDN browser cookie contract. This does not claim a live browser attack simulation.
